source_trace: The viewer collects every finite DiagnosticsStore render/ value into a vector per string path, requiring at least half the requested sample-frame count for each path. It does not compare a measurement timestamp or frame identity.

The pinned bevy_diagnostic Diagnostic::value returns the latest history entry. Bevy render sync adds a diagnostic when a mapped frame callback is available, using an Instant at sync; the capture consumer does not inspect that Instant. If a value stays unchanged between collection ticks, the same stored measurement can be counted more than once, including across mode boundaries. No actual delayed or stale sample has been observed.

The viewer separately summarizes each path and sums every summary whose path ends elapsed_gpu; the sum feeds limiting_p95_ms and the measured 60 FPS gate. Pinned bevy_render constructs diagnostic paths from same-thread parent spans and marks available timestamp duration (end−begin) times timestamp_period_ns / 1e6 as milliseconds. This establishes how native paths can be nested, not which supported spans actually occur or are disjoint on any host.

The native documentation claims a platform restriction for timestamp queries, while the implementation checks device features and query limits. Treat the comment as source evidence with possible drift, not proof that a particular backend cannot provide timestamps.

One hypothetical arithmetic example, not measured data: on 20 aligned frames disjoint pass A takes10 ms only on frame1 and pass B takes10 ms only on frame2, with all other values0. The code’s rounded P95 index is18; each per-path sorted P95 is0, while sorted per-frame totals have 18 zeros and two tens, so total P95 is10 ms. Thus sum-of-P95 is not generally P95-of-sum even with disjoint synchronized paths.
